model_and_quantifiers.common_universe: For integer t>=1 and D=2^t, groups g are all F_2^t; resources are all pairs (a,b) in F_2^(2t). Each group has every indexed state ell in F_2^t, with S_(g,ell)={(a,b): b_i+g_i a_i=ell_i for all i}. Each state has D distinct resources, each of weight 1/D.
model_and_quantifiers.free_input: A chooses an arbitrary vector ell(g) separately for each group and an arbitrary subset A_g of S_(g,ell(g)); the subsets are pairwise disjoint. The vector coordinate ell_i(g) may depend on all bits of g. Partial bundles need not be Cartesian, and resources may remain idle.
model_and_quantifiers.consistent_output: B must admit one common family f=(f_i:F_2->F_2) with ell_i^B(g)=f_i(g_i) for every group simultaneously. B may choose f after seeing the complete input A and t; it may change every selected state and every bundle, and need not retain any particular input resource. Bundles remain arbitrary subsets and resources remain indivisible.
model_and_quantifiers.value: v(A)=min_g |A_g|/D, and the same normalization applies to B.
model_and_quantifiers.contract_to_negate: For each fixed theta in [0,1), there is no constant c>0 such that for every t>=1 and every free A on this same menu with v(A)>=theta, some consistent B on that menu has v(B)>=c v(A).
model_and_quantifiers.negation_proved: For every fixed theta in [0,1) and c>0, there exist t>=1 and one free A_t with v(A_t)>=theta such that every same-menu consistent B has v(B)<c v(A_t). No algorithm or time bound is assumed.

notation_change_assessment.actual_change: At the generic support definition in the current sparse-audit review, b_i+g_i a_i=ell_i(g_i) was corrected to b_i+g_i a_i=ell_i. The frozen original already uses ell_i. The cyclic choice ell_i(g)=g_(i+1) is preserved.
notation_change_assessment.why_no_constraint_is_added: S_(g,ell) first defines the entire state list with ell as a free vector index. A later state-selection rule chooses ell(g) and may use the whole g. Writing the component ell_i in the generic support equation neither imposes a common fixed ell for all groups nor factors ell_i(g) through g_i. Only the separate quota problem introduces ell_i(g)=f_i(g_i).
notation_change_assessment.cyclic_check: For t>=2, the cyclic rule ell_i(g)=g_(i+1) takes different values on groups with the same g_i, so it is a legitimate free selection and is generally outside the consistent class. For t=1 the cyclic rule happens to be local, and both values are 1/2; this does not affect the large-t separation.
notation_change_assessment.verdict: Notation-only correction restores the intended complete-menu definition and preserves all mathematics used by this implication.

proof_obligations.derivation: Choose ell_i(g)=g_(i+1) with cyclic indices and A_g={(a,b): a!=1^t, b_i=g_(i+1)+g_i a_i for all i}. Each group has exactly D-1 resources. If a resource belongs to both A_g and A_h, delta=g+h obeys delta_(i+1)=a_i delta_i. Some a_r=0; propagate delta_(r+1)=0 around the full cycle to obtain delta=0 and g=h. Thus these are real disjoint bundles with v(A_t)=(D-1)/D. No relabeling or resource privatization occurs.
proof_obligations.minimal_use_in_implication: The obstruction needs this achieved high-value lower bound, not the free upper bound or the ordinary scheduling OPT.

proof_obligations.derivation: Fix any common f and set u_i=f_i(0), w_i=f_i(1). Apply the same translation tau_f to every true resource: a_i_prime=a_i+u_i+w_i and b_i_prime=b_i+u_i. This bijection is independent of g. Over F_2, b_i_prime+g_i a_i_prime=f_i(g_i)+u_i+g_i(u_i+w_i)=0 for both g_i=0 and g_i=1. Therefore the whole selected graph for f is sent to the zero-label selected graph at once. Cardinality, weights, group identity, all adjacency and disjointness are preserved. The map may depend on f but is never chosen separately for different groups. Hence each fixed f has the same entire feasible integer quota spectrum.

In each coordinate the two selected lines have a unique common resource C and one distinct exclusive resource E_0 or E_1 each. Their product union is exactly {C,E_0,E_1}^t of size 3^t. This holds for every fixed f by direct two-line reasoning or by tau_f. For any disjoint output let s=min_g |B_g|, an integer. Then D s <= sum_g |B_g| <= 3^t, so s <= k_t=floor(3^t/2^t)=floor((3/2)^t), and v(B)<=k_t/D. Arbitrary-shaped partial bundles and discarding resources are already included.

For a used resource u with h common-symbol coordinates, exactly 2^h groups are compatible. Give each compatible edge weight 2^(-h), so each resource supplies one unit total. Each group receives product_i(1+1/2)=rho_t=(3/2)^t. Therefore every group subset H, including non-product subsets, has |N(H)|>=rho_t |H|>=k_t |H|. Split each group into k_t slots with identical neighbors. For any slot subset Z, if H is its touched group set then N(Z)=N(H) and |Z|<=k_t |H|<=|N(Z)|; the empty case is trivial. Hall gives an ordinary integer matching covering every slot. Each group receives exactly k_t distinct resources, and resources are not shared across groups. Thus the exact value k_t/D is attained. An equivalent integer-capacity flow enforces source->group k_t, group->resource 1, resource->sink 1. Fractional evidence proves Hall; it is not treated as an indivisible allocation.
proof_obligations.role_in_obstruction: The exact lower bound confirms the quota source. The repair contradiction itself only uses the uniform upper bound from the previous obligation.

proof_obligations.derivation: Every permitted consistent output B has at least one common family f witnessing its consistency. Apply the per-fixed-f upper bound to that actual f. Because the bound k_t/D is independent of f, choosing f as an arbitrary function of the whole A and t cannot improve it. In symbols max_f V_obl(t;f)=k_t/D. This also covers complete reselection of all bundles; no subset-of-input or same-state restriction is used.

For fixed theta in [0,1) and c>0, choose one integer t>=1 with 2^(-t)<=1-theta and 2(3/4)^t<c. Both conditions can hold simultaneously because 1-theta>0 and the two exponential terms tend to zero. For example t=max{1,ceil(log_2(1/(1-theta))),floor(ln(2/c)/ln(4/3))+1} suffices. Then v(A_t)=1-2^(-t)>=theta. Since D-1>0, every permitted B satisfies v(B)/v(A_t)<=R_t=k_t/(D-1)<=(3/4)^t/(1-2^(-t))<=2(3/4)^t<c. Consequently every B has v(B)<c v(A_t). The strict inequality follows from the strict choice of the second bound, including c>=1 or theta=0.

Let epsilon_t=(3/2)^t-k_t with 0<=epsilon_t<1. Then k_t/D=(3/4)^t-epsilon_t/2^t. Thus 0<=(3/4)^t-k_t/D<2^(-t), and dividing by the positive continuous comparison value (3/4)^t gives relative error epsilon_t/(3/2)^t<(2/3)^t. Neither error formula removes the integer floor or identifies this menu value with an ordinary-UM makespan.

The free source supplies the actual high-valued input family; the quota source supplies an upper bound for every allowed consistent output on precisely the same menu. Together they prove the complete target quantifier statement, even when only output existence is demanded. The quota bound alone does not supply a high-valued free input; the free witness alone does not bound all consistent outputs. Preserve the single two-source ALL edge. The Hall lower-bound proof and free scheduling theorem are stronger source content, not hidden additional premises for the final ratio argument.

whole_result: {free v3 achieved witness, quota v1 uniform upper bound} jointly imply: for every fixed theta in [0,1) and c>0, some t and same-menu free A_t satisfy v(A_t)>=theta while all same-menu coordinate-consistent B satisfy v(B)<c v(A_t). This covers arbitrary reselection of the entire common function family and all bundles and requires no algorithm.
limits: The same menu means the same groups, true resources, indexed-state lists and weights. A compiler that changes these objects or proves a different guarantee is outside this obstruction.
Theta=1 gives no high-valued input on this finite-t family because V_free(t)=1-2^(-t)<1. The proof does not negate that empty-domain contract.
A preservation factor c_t allowed to decay with t is outside the uniform-positive-constant claim; the maximum ratio on A_t is exactly R_t.

The coordinate restriction is extra state-selection semantics. It has not been encoded as a necessary property of every low-load ordinary scheduling solution; quota values cannot be substituted as a NO bound for the unrestricted ordinary matrix.
Historical t=1..4 sparse audits are finite evidence and are not used as the all-t proof. No historical run, new blind review, source hardness, novelty or general UM conclusion is claimed.
